question: What are net interest income and the net interest margin, and how did they change?

answer.summary: Net interest income (NII) was $89.3 billion in FY2023, up 34%, driven by higher rates, the impact of First Republic, and higher revolving balances in Card Services, partially offset by lower Markets NII and lower average deposit balances [T00960]. NII excluding Markets was $90.0 billion, up 44% [T00960]. A net interest margin value is not in the retrieved evidence; the filing only defines 'deposit margin' as NII as a percentage of average deposits without giving a value [T04535], and the separate 'Net margin %' (net income/revenues) was 31.3% in FY2023 vs 29.3% in FY2022 (+207 bps) [F13515][F13514] — a different metric, not net interest margin.

key_numbers.metric: Net margin % (net income/revenues; NOT net interest margin)
Net margin % (net income/revenues; NOT net interest margin)

drivers: NII up 34% to $89.3B: higher rates, the impact of First Republic, and higher revolving balances in Card Services [T00960]
Offsets (moved against the increase): lower Markets net interest income and lower average deposit balances [T00960]
NII excluding Markets rose 44% to $90.0B, implying Markets NII declined [T00960]
No percentage-of-total-change attribution is provided in the retrieved evidence for these components
risks_and_red_flags: Lower Markets NII and lower average deposit balances partially offset the NII increase [T00960]
NII includes the impact of First Republic, an acquisition-related contribution that may not repeat [T00960]
